goalTextEn: Can talk about yourself using basic personal and job information.
goalTextKr: 기본적인 개인 정보와 직무 정보를 사용해 자기소개를 할 수 있다.

introduce.goalEn: Can talk about yourself using basic personal and job information.
introduce.goalKr: 기본적인 개인 정보와 직무 정보를 사용해 자기소개를 할 수 있다.
introduce.situationEn: It's your first time meeting your teammates at a new company. Everyone is taking turns introducing themselves. Now it's your turn!
introduce.situationKr: 새 회사에서 팀원들을 처음 만납니다. 모두가 차례대로 자기소개를 하고 있습니다. 당신 차례입니다!

tutorNotes.text: "Today, we'll practice introducing yourself at work."
Read the lesson goal aloud. Ask the student to repeat.
"Is it clear?"
Read the situation.
"Let's go to the next part."
Encourage the student to speak in short, clear sentences.

vocabulary.definition: a business organization where people work
your job title or role in a company
the amount of time you have worked or lived somewhere

pronunciation.instruction: Let's practice hearing the difference between /l/ and /r/.

tutorNotes.text: "Let's look at patterns used when introducing yourself."
Read the first pattern. Ask the student to repeat.
"Use this to say your name."
Read the second pattern. Ask the student to repeat.
"Use this to say where you work."
Read the third pattern. Ask the student to repeat.
"Use this to say where you are from."
Read the fourth pattern. Ask the student to repeat.
"Use this to say your position."
Read the fifth pattern. Ask the student to repeat.
"Use this to say how long you have worked there."
"Do you have any questions about the patterns?"
"Let's go to the next page."

understand.instruction: Fill in the blanks with the correct pattern. Then practice the pattern drills.
understand.instructionKr: 빈칸에 올바른 패턴을 넣으세요. 그런 다음 패턴 드릴을 연습하세요.

patternDrills.label: Saying your work experience
patternDrills.template: I have worked here for ___ years.

examples.en: I have worked here for 1 year.
I have worked here for 2 years.
I have worked here for 3 years.
I have worked here for 4 years.
I have worked here for 5 years.

tutorNotes.text: "Now, let's work on comprehension."
Read the instruction.
"First, let's practice the sentence patterns."
Read each pattern heading, then continue the drill. Ask the student to repeat and complete the blank with real information if possible.
For lower-level students, give one model sentence first and let them change only one part.
"Do you have any questions? ...Let's go to the next part!"
"Now, let's look at the word bank."
Read each word, then ask the student to repeat.
Correct the student's pronunciation errors if needed.
For lower-level students, read the word and the definition, then ask the student to repeat.
"Do you have any questions? ...Let's go to the next part!"
"Now, let's practice the /l/ and /r/ sounds."
Practice the /l/ words first, then the /r/ words. Ask the student to repeat.
Teach the student how to pronounce /l/ and /r/ with mouth and tongue position if needed.
Correct mispronounced words after reading.
"Do you have any questions? ...Let's go to the next part."

steps.title: Step 1 — Repeat After Me
steps.instructionEn: Listen and repeat each self-introduction sentence.
steps.content:
1. Hi, I'm Minji.
2. I work at Global Corp.
3. I am a sales assistant.
4. I am from Busan.
5. I have worked here for 2 years.
6. Nice to meet you!

tutorNotes.text: "Let's practice today's introduction sentences."
Read the instruction.
Read each sentence. Ask the student to repeat.
Adjust speed according to the student's level.
Correct mispronounced words after reading.
"Nice! Let's go to the next part!"

steps.title: Step 2 — Fill in Your Introduction
steps.instructionEn: Complete these sentences with your own information.

tutorNotes.text: "Now, complete the sentences with your own information."
Read the instruction.
Ask the student to fill in each blank with their real information, then read the full introduction aloud.
If the student does not work at a company, they can say "I study at ..." or "I work from home."
"Nice! Let's go to the next part!"

steps.title: Step 3 — Dialogue Practice
steps.instructionEn: Practice the dialogue with your tutor. You are the new team member.
steps.instructionKr: 선생님과 대화를 연습하세요. 당신은 새로운 팀원입니다.

dialogue.en: Hi! Welcome to the team. I'm Grace.
dialogue.kr: 안녕하세요! 팀에 오신 것을 환영합니다. 저는 그레이스입니다.

dialogue.en: Hi, I'm (your name). Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you too. Where are you from?
How long have you worked here?
I have worked here for (number) years.

tutorNotes.text: "Now, let's practice the dialogue."
Read the instruction.
"I will read the tutor parts. You will read the student parts."
Do it once while reading, then once again without looking at the screen if possible.
If time permits, switch roles so the student practices asking questions too.
"Nice! Let's go to the next part!"

steps.title: Step 4 — Free Introduction
steps.instructionEn: Introduce yourself to your tutor without looking at any notes. Try to say at least 5 sentences.
steps.instructionKr: 메모를 보지 않고 선생님에게 자기소개를 하세요. 5문장 이상 말해 보세요.
steps.content:
Include:
- Your name
- Where you're from
- Where you work
- Your position
- How many years you have worked there

tutorNotes.text: "Now, introduce yourself without looking at your notes."
Read the instruction.
Let the student speak freely. Note any errors but do not interrupt.
After they finish, give feedback on pronunciation and grammar.
If the student stops early, prompt with one short question such as "Where are you from?"
"Nice! Let's go to the next part!"

challenge.scenarioEn: You joined a new project team. Introduce yourself to three new teammates. Your tutor will play each teammate and ask you questions.
challenge.scenarioKr: 새로운 프로젝트 팀에 합류했습니다. 3명의 새 팀원에게 자기소개를 하세요. 선생님이 각 팀원 역할을 하며 질문합니다.

tutorNotes.text: "Now let's do simulation"
"First please read the Key Expressions. You may use the Key Expressions in the Simulation."
Read the simulation.
"Is it clear?" ...Now let's start our roleplay!
Use the prompt questions to guide the roleplay.
Give feedback after finishing.
This must be a real-life simulation, distinct from Practice. Corrections should only be done after the exercise.
Hi! I'm Alex. What's your name?
Nice to meet you. Where are you from?
Where do you work?
What is your position?
How long have you worked there?

discussion.instructionEn: Choose one category, then answer the questions.

categories.title: FIRST DAY AT WORK
questions: What did you say on your first day?
Who was the first person you met?

categories.title: YOUR IDEAL INTRODUCTION
questions: What information do you always include?
Do you prefer short or long introductions?

categories.title: MEETING NEW PEOPLE
questions: Do you like meeting new people?
What's a good way to start a conversation?
What questions do you ask new people?

tutorNotes.text: "Now, let's have a discussion."
Read the instruction.
Ask the student to choose a category.
You can ask follow-up questions and have a natural conversation with the student until the time for feedback.

feedback.goalReviewEn: Can talk about yourself using basic personal and job information.
feedback.goalReviewKr: 기본적인 개인 정보와 직무 정보를 사용해 자기소개를 할 수 있다.
feedback.feedbackTemplate:
*OVERALL SCORE*
Overall: (score)
- comment

*Speaking Fluency*
Fluency:
- Could introduce themselves smoothly: (yes/partially/no)
- Spoke in full sentences: (yes/no)

*Vocabulary / Phrases*
Vocabulary:
- word/phrase
- word/phrase

*Pronunciation*
Pronunciation:
- mispronounced word
- mispronounced word

tutorNotes.text: "It's the end of the lesson. Great job!"
Ask the student to read the lesson goal.
"Were you able to achieve today's lesson goal?"
Fill in and send the feedback template via chat.
Practice mispronounced words with the student.
Encourage the next lesson naturally.
